message: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.
status_detail: EBS Default Encryption is not activated.

analytic.name: EBS default encryption is enabled

finding_info.desc: **EBS** uses `encryption by default` at the account and region level, ensuring new volumes, snapshots, and AMI-backed volumes are automatically encrypted with a chosen **KMS key**
finding_info.title: EBS default encryption is enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc: Enable `EBS encryption by default` in every region and select a **customer-managed KMS key**. Apply **least privilege** to key use, rotate keys, and monitor access. Enforce encrypted volume creation with organizational guardrails and secure templates as **defense in depth**.

risk_details: Without `encryption by default`, data on new **EBS volumes** and **snapshots** may be stored in plaintext. A compromised account or mis-shared snapshot can expose disk contents, enabling data exfiltration, offline analysis, and loss of **confidentiality**.

message: EBS Snapshot vol-09a5a1cf5838936ca is encrypted.
status_detail: EBS Snapshot vol-09a5a1cf5838936ca is encrypted.

analytic.name: EBS volume is encrypted

finding_info.desc:
**EBS volumes** are assessed for **encryption at rest** using **AWS KMS**.

The finding identifies volumes whose `encrypted` state is disabled, meaning data is stored unencrypted on block storage.
finding_info.title: EBS volume is encrypted
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
Effects/Data Exposure

remediation.desc:
Encrypt all EBS volumes and enable `encryption by default` for new volumes and snapshot copies.

Apply **least privilege** to KMS keys, restrict snapshot sharing, and enforce **defense in depth** with policies and templates that prevent creation of unencrypted storage.

risk_details:
Unencrypted volumes or snapshots can be copied, shared, or recovered and reveal raw data, undermining **confidentiality**.

Adversaries with host or account access can read disks offline, harvest secrets, or alter system images, affecting **integrity** and enabling **lateral movement**.

message: EBS Volume vol-09a5a1cf5838936ca is not protected by a backup plan.
status_detail: EBS Volume vol-09a5a1cf5838936ca is not protected by a backup plan.

analytic.name: EBS volume is protected by a backup plan

finding_info.desc: **EBS volumes** are evaluated for coverage by an **AWS Backup plan**, whether explicitly targeted or included via broad resource selection, confirming scheduled, policy-driven backups exist for the volume.
finding_info.title: EBS volume is protected by a backup plan
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc: Include all critical EBS volumes in standardized **AWS Backup** plans aligned to your `RPO`/`RTO`. Use tags for automatic assignment, enable cross-Region/account copies, apply **Vault Lock** for WORM retention, encrypt with KMS, enforce least-privilege access, and regularly test restores to verify integrity.

risk_details: Absent backup coverage, volumes face **data loss**, weakened **integrity**, and reduced **availability**. Deletion or corruption-whether accidental or malicious-can leave no recovery path, causing prolonged outages, failed point-in-time restoration, unmet retention needs, and harder incident response.

status_detail: Snapshots not found for the EBS volume vol-09a5a1cf5838936ca.

finding_info.title: EBS volume has at least one snapshot
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Effects/Data Destruction

remediation.desc:
Establish automated, policy-based **EBS snapshot** coverage for all volumes aligned to business `RPO/RTO`.
- Schedule regular snapshots with retention controls
- Encrypt snapshots and enforce **least privilege** access
- Replicate to another Region/account for DR
- Periodically test restores and document procedures

message: IMDSv2 is not enabled by default for EC2 instances.
status_detail: IMDSv2 is not enabled by default for EC2 instances.

analytic.name: IMDSv2 is required by default for EC2 instances at the account level

finding_info.desc: **EC2 account IMDS defaults** with `http_tokens`=`required` ensure new instances in the Region use **IMDSv2** by default and disable IMDSv1. *Existing instances keep their current setting.*
finding_info.title: IMDSv2 is required by default for EC2 instances at the account level
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
TTPs/Credential Access

remediation.desc: Enforce **IMDSv2** at the account level in every Region by setting `http_tokens` to `required`. Add guardrails with **SCP/IAM conditions**. Standardize AMIs and launch templates to require tokens, validate workload compatibility, and apply **least privilege** to instance roles for defense in depth. *For containers*, prefer hop limit `2`.

risk_details: Without a default of **IMDSv2**, new instances may enable **IMDSv1**, exposing metadata via simple HTTP. SSRF or proxy misconfigs can steal **temporary IAM credentials**, enabling data exfiltration (confidentiality), unauthorized API changes (integrity), and lateral movement that can disrupt services (availability).

message: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 does not have detailed monitoring enabled.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 does not have detailed monitoring enabled.

analytic.name: EC2 instance has detailed monitoring enabled

finding_info.desc:
**EC2 instances** are assessed for **CloudWatch detailed monitoring**, indicating whether 1-minute metrics collection is enabled.

Instances lacking this setting provide only 5-minute metrics.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance has detailed monitoring enabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Enable **detailed monitoring** to collect `1-minute` metrics on critical instances. Use **defense in depth**: baseline normal behavior, create alerts for anomalies, and correlate metrics with logs and traces. Review dashboards regularly. *If costs matter*, prioritize production, internet-facing, and autoscaling fleets.

risk_details:
Without 1-minute metrics, visibility drops, delaying detection of:
- Sudden CPU/network/disk spikes affecting **availability**
- **Malicious workloads** (crypto-mining, brute force)
- **Data exfiltration** patterns
Slower detection expands blast radius, raising incident impact and response cost.

message: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 has IMDSv2 enabled and required.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 has IMDSv2 enabled and required.

analytic.name: EC2 instance requires IMDSv2 or has the instance metadata service disabled

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for **IMDSv2 enforcement**: metadata endpoint enabled with `http_tokens: required`, or metadata service fully disabled (`http_endpoint: disabled`).
finding_info.title: EC2 instance requires IMDSv2 or has the instance metadata service disabled
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
TTPs/Credential Access

remediation.desc:
Apply defense in depth:
- Require **IMDSv2** tokens on all instances (`http_tokens: required`)
- Disable metadata where not needed (`http_endpoint: disabled`)
- Minimize hop limit to `1` when feasible
- Update SDKs/apps for IMDSv2
- Restrict instance profile permissions (least privilege)
- Block metadata access from untrusted workloads

risk_details: Permitting **IMDSv1** or optional tokens lets SSRF or compromised workloads retrieve **temporary IAM credentials**, impacting confidentiality and integrity. Stolen role creds can drive **privilege escalation**, unauthorized data access, and lateral movement across AWS resources.

Remote exploits or misconfigurations can steal credentials via the **instance metadata service**, enabling unauthorized API calls, data exfiltration, and lateral movement, impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

message: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 is managed by Systems Manager.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 is managed by Systems Manager.

analytic.name: EC2 instance is managed by AWS Systems Manager or not running

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are assessed for enrollment as **Systems Manager managed nodes**. Running instances lacking Systems Manager registration are marked as unmanaged; instances in `stopped`, `terminated`, or `pending` states are noted separately.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance is managed by AWS Systems Manager or not running
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Patch Management

remediation.desc: Enroll all instances as **Systems Manager managed nodes**. Prefer **Session Manager** over SSH/RDP, restrict inbound admin ports, and use **least privilege** roles. Ensure connectivity to SSM endpoints (or private endpoints), automate patching and inventory, and monitor activity for defense-in-depth.

risk_details: Unmanaged instances lack centralized patching, inventory, and secure remote access. This increases exposure to brute force on SSH/RDP, delayed patching, and poor visibility. Exploits can enable lateral movement and persistence, degrading confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

message: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 is not older than 180 days (0 days).
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 is not older than 180 days (0 days).

analytic.name: EC2 instance is not older than the configured maximum age or is not running

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for age while in `running` state. Instances launched beyond the configurable limit (`max_ec2_instance_age_in_days`, default `180`) are flagged as older than the allowed lifetime. Stopped instances are ignored.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance is not older than the configured maximum age or is not running
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Software and Configuration Checks/Patch Management

remediation.desc:
Adopt **short-lived, patched workloads**:
- Rebuild regularly from hardened, updated images; rotate AMIs
- Use centralized patch management and vulnerability scanning
- Retire or modernize legacy hosts; tag for lifecycle
- Apply **least privilege** and **defense in depth** to limit blast radius

Adjust `max_ec2_instance_age_in_days` to match policy.

risk_details:
Long-lived instances often run **unpatched OS and agents**, enabling:
- Exploitation of known CVEs  loss of confidentiality
- Privilege escalation and tampering  integrity compromise
- Malware/crypto-mining and instability  reduced availability

Aged hosts also drift from baselines and impede response.

message: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 virtualization type is set to HVM.
status_detail: EC2 Instance i-08adc39bb44195755 virtualization type is set to HVM.

analytic.name: EC2 instance virtualization type is HVM

finding_info.desc: **EC2 instances** are evaluated for their virtualization mode. Instances with `virtualization_type` set to `paravirtual` are identified; those using **HVM** are recognized as hardware-assisted virtualization.
finding_info.title: EC2 instance virtualization type is HVM
types: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices

remediation.desc: Standardize on **HVM/Nitro**. Migrate PV workloads to HVM AMIs and current instance families; ensure support for `ENA` and `NVMe`, current kernels, and hardened configs. Apply **defense in depth** and **least privilege**. Use immutable images with staged testing, then retire PV images to prevent drift and regressions.

risk_details: Using **paravirtual (PV)** weakens isolation versus **HVM/Nitro** and blocks features like `ENA` and `NVMe`. Confidentiality and integrity can suffer due to reliance on legacy hypercalls/drivers; availability and performance may degrade under load, increasing exposure to kernel/driver exploits and noisy-neighbor impacts.

remediation.desc:
Apply **least privilege** and **segmentation**:
- Limit rules to required ports, protocols, and sources
- Split workloads into dedicated security groups per role
- Prefer SG-to-SG references over broad CIDRs
- Regularly review, deduplicate, and remove stale rules
- Layer controls (NACLs, private endpoints) for **defense in depth**

risk_details: **Rule sprawl** weakens **least privilege**: large rule sets can hide overly permissive entries, exposing services to the Internet or unintended peers. This enables unauthorized access, data exfiltration, and lateral movement, impacting **confidentiality** and **integrity**, and can threaten **availability** via abuse of exposed services.
